Figure 1:Spatial state representations from streaming egocentric observations.A moving observer builds an internal spatial representation from partial
views of an environment.L1(spatial structure) captures scene geometry and object
identity across views.L2(object persistence) retains the observer-relative
locations of previously seen objects after they leave the field of view.L3(predictive spatial update) anticipates what the
observer would see after an action or a sequence of actions.L4(actionability) uses the represented state and a
specified goal to select an action that makes progress toward that goal.

Figure 3:Probing four spatial capabilities.Probe inputs and
targets at each level: prefix features alone (L1), plus an object query
(L2), ego-motions and an isolated future feature (L3), or a goal frame
and an action (L4).

Figure 7:Layer–prefix structure of instance identity and object persistence.The four panels show instance identity (top) and object persistence
(bottom) for VideoMAE (left) and V-JEPA2 (right) across extraction
layers and prefix lengths. Colors are normalized within each panel and
therefore describe within-model structure rather than absolute
cross-model accuracy; raw values accompany the heatmaps. No probe was
trained on block 0 of either model, so it is not shown.

Figure 9:Spatial readout across generation coordinates.Top: each model at the early (dark) and the late (light) scheduler index
at block 20, averaged over prefixes; arrows give the better direction,
and the values are listed inTable12. Bottom: the
better coordinate for every layer–prefix pair, E (early) or L (late),
grouped by block.
